title: Chapter 1 — Carnivora
description: Despite the name, Carnivora is defined by shared ancestry and skull anatomy, not diet. The order includes dedicated meat-eaters like cats and wolves, but also omnivores like bears and raccoons, and even the bamboo-eating giant panda.

children.name: Prionailurus
children.description: Prionailurus — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Prionailurus bengalensis
children.description: The leopard cat is a small wild cat with dark spots on the tawny-coloured body and limbs. It has two dark stripes running from the eyes to the ears and smaller white streaks running from the eyes to the nose, and two to four rows of elongated spots along its back. Its tail is about half the size of its head-to-body length.

children.name: Prionailurus iriomotensis
children.description: The Iriomote cat is a subspecies of the leopard cat that lives exclusively on the Japanese island of Iriomote.

children.name: Prionailurus planiceps
children.description: The flat-headed cat is a small wild cat with short reddish-brown fur. Its head is elongated, and its ears are rounded. Its slender body is 41 to 50 cm long with a tail of 13 to 15 cm, and it weighs 1.5 to 2.5 kg.

children.name: Prionailurus rubiginosus
children.description: The rusty-spotted cat is one of the cat family's smallest members. It is native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka. Since 2016, it has been listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List as the global population is affected by loss and destruction of its prime habitat, deciduous forests.

children.name: Prionailurus viverrinus
children.description: The fishing cat is a medium-sized wild cat of South and Southeast Asia. It has a deep yellowish-grey fur with black lines and spots. Adults have a head-to-body length of 57 to 78 cm, with a 20 to 30 cm long tail.

children.name: Leopardus
children.description: Leopardus — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Leopardus braccatus
children.description: The Pantanal cat is a Pampas cat subspecies, a small wild cat native to South America. It is named after the Pantanal wetlands in central South America, where it inhabits mainly grassland, shrubland, savannas and deciduous forests.

children.name: Leopardus colocolo
children.description: The Pampas cat is a small wild cat native to South America. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List as habitat conversion and destruction may cause the population to decline in the future.

children.name: Leopardus geoffroyi
children.description: Geoffroy's cat (Leopardus geoffroyi) is a small wild cat native to the southern and central regions of South America..

children.name: Leopardus guigna
children.description: The kodkod, also called güiña, is the smallest felid species native to the Americas. It lives primarily in central and southern Chile, as well as marginally in adjoining areas of Argentina. Between 1996 and 2002, it was listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List as the total population was thought to be fewer than 10,000 mature individuals; it is threatened by persecution, habitat loss and prey base.

children.name: Leopardus guttulus
children.description: Leopardus guttulus, the southern tigrina or southern tiger cat, is a small wild cat species native to Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay.

children.name: Leopardus jacobitus
children.description: The Andean mountain cat (Leopardus jacobita) is a small wild cat native to the high Andes that has been listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List because fewer than 1,500 individuals are thought to exist in the wild.

children.name: Leopardus pajeros
children.description: The Pampas cat is a small wild cat native to South America. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List as habitat conversion and destruction may cause the population to decline in the future.

children.name: Leopardus pardalis
children.description: The ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) is a medium-sized spotted wild cat that reaches 40–50 cm (16–20 in) at the shoulders and weighs between 7 and 15.5 kg (15 and 34 lb) on average..

children.name: Leopardus tigrinus
children.description: The oncilla, also known as the northern tiger cat, little spotted cat, and tigrillo, is a small spotted cat ranging from Central America to central Brazil. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, and the population is threatened by deforestation and conversion of habitat to agricultural land.

children.name: Leopardus wiedii
children.description: The margay (Leopardus wiedii) is a small wild cat native to Mexico, Central and South America..

children.name: Caracal
children.description: Caracal — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Caracal caracal
children.description: The caracal (Caracal caracal) is a wild cat native to Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, and arid areas of Pakistan and northwestern India..

children.name: Felis
children.description: Felis — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Felis antediluviana
children.description: Promegantereon is an extinct genus of machairodont from the Miocene of Europe..

children.name: Felis atrox
children.description: The American lion (Panthera atrox (), with the species name meaning "savage" or "cruel", also called the North American lion) is an extinct pantherine cat native to North America during the Late Pleistocene from around 129,000 to 13,100 years ago.

children.name: Felis attica
children.description: Pristifelis is an extinct genus of feline from the late Miocene..

children.name: Felis bieti
children.description: The Chinese mountain cat (Felis bieti), also known as Chinese desert cat and Chinese steppe cat, is a small wild Felis species with sand-coloured fur, faint dark stripes on the face and legs and black tipped ears.

children.name: Felis catus
children.description: The cat, also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal. It is an obligate carnivore, requiring a predominantly meat-based diet. Its retractable claws are adapted to killing small prey species such as mice and rats.

children.name: Felis chaus
children.description: The jungle cat (Felis chaus), also called reed cat and swamp cat, is a medium-sized cat native from the Eastern Mediterranean region and the Caucasus to parts of Central, South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Felis lanea
children.description: The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.

children.name: Felis lunensis
children.description: Felis lunensis, or the Martelli's cat is an extinct felid of the subfamily Felinae.

children.name: Felis manul
children.description: Pallas's cat (Otocolobus manul), also called manul, is a small wild cat with long and dense light grey fur, and rounded ears set low on the sides of the head..

children.name: Felis margarita
children.description: The sand cat (Felis margarita) is a small wild cat that inhabits sandy and stony deserts far from water sources.

children.name: Felis nigripes
children.description: The black-footed cat (Felis nigripes), also called the small-spotted cat, is the smallest wild cat in Africa, having a head-and-body length of 35–52 cm (14–20 in)..

children.name: Felis pardoides
children.description: Puma pardoides is an extinct prehistoric cat belonging to the genus Puma known from fossils found in Europe and West Asia during the late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene epochs, spanning from around 3 million to 860,000 years ago.

children.name: Felis silvestris
children.description: The European wildcat (Felis silvestris) is a small wildcat species that was described in the late 18th century.

children.name: Neofelis
children.description: Neofelis — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Neofelis diardi
children.description: The Sunda clouded leopard (Neofelis diardi) is a medium-sized wild cat native to Borneo and Sumatra..

children.name: Neofelis nebulosa
children.description: The clouded leopard (Neofelis nebulosa), also called mainland clouded leopard, is a wild cat that has large dusky-grey blotches and irregular spots and stripes reminiscent of clouds.

children.name: Pardofelis
children.description: Pardofelis — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Pardofelis marmorata
children.description: The marbled cat (Pardofelis marmorata) is a small wild cat native from the eastern Himalayas to Southeast Asia, where it inhabits forests up to an elevation of .

children.name: Catopuma
children.description: Catopuma — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Catopuma badia
children.description: The bay cat (Catopuma badia), also known as the Bornean bay cat, is a small wild cat endemic to the island of Borneo that appears to be relatively rare compared to sympatric wild cats, based on the paucity of historical, as well as recent records.

children.name: Catopuma temminckii
children.description: The Asian golden cat (Catopuma temminckii) is a medium-sized wild cat native to the northeastern Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Puma
children.description: Puma — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Puma concolor
children.description: The cougar ( KOO-gər; Puma concolor), also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large feline native to the Americas..

children.name: Puma yagouaroundi
children.description: The jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi);  or  is a wild cat native to the Americas..

children.name: Leptailurus

children.name: Leptailurus serval
children.description: The serval (Leptailurus serval) is a wild small cat native to Africa..

children.name: Uncia

children.name: Uncia uncia
children.description: The snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.

children.name: Lynx
children.description: Lynx — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Lynx canadensis
children.description: The Canada lynx (Lynx canadensis) or Canadian lynx is one of the four living species in the genus Lynx.

children.name: Lynx lynx
children.description: The Eurasian lynx is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx. It is widely distributed from Northern, Central and Eastern Europe to Central Asia and Siberia, the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalayas. It inhabits temperate and boreal forests up to an elevation of 5,500 m (18,000 ft).

children.name: Lynx pardinus
children.description: The Iberian lynx is one of four extant species of Lynx, a genus of medium-sized wild cats. It is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Fossils suggest that it has been present in Iberia since the end of the Early Pleistocene around 1 million years ago.

children.name: Lynx rufus
children.description: The bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx..

children.name: Lynx spelaea
children.description: The cave lynx or Mediterranean cave lynx (Lynx spelaeus or Lynx pardinus spelaeus) is an extinct felid species that lived during the Pleistocene.

children.name: Acinonyx
children.description: Acinonyx — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Acinonyx aicha
children.description: Acinonyx aicha is an extinct felid species belonging to the genus Acinonyx.

children.name: Acinonyx jubatus
children.description: The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx..

children.name: Acinonyx pardinensis
children.description: Acinonyx pardinensis, sometimes called the giant cheetah, is an extinct felid species belonging to the genus Acinonyx, closely related to the cheetah, native to Eurasia from Late Pliocene to the early Middle Pleistocene epoch from around 3 million to around 500,000 years ago.

children.name: Proailurus
children.description: Proailurus — a genus of cats in the family Felidae.

children.name: Proailurus lemanensis
children.description: Proailurus is an extinct felid genus that lived in Europe and Asia approximately 25–30.8 million years ago in the Late Oligocene and Miocene..

children.description: Homotherium is an extinct genus of scimitar-toothed cat belonging to the extinct subfamily Machairodontinae that inhabited North America, Eurasia, and Africa, as well as possibly South America during the Pliocene and Pleistocene epochs from around 4 million to 12,000 years ago..

children.name: Homotherium venezuelensis
children.description: Homotherium is an extinct genus of scimitar-toothed cat belonging to the extinct subfamily Machairodontinae that inhabited North America, Eurasia, and Africa, as well as possibly South America during the Pliocene and Pleistocene epochs from around 4 million to 12,000 years ago..

children.name: Megantereon whitei
children.description: Megantereon is an extinct genus of prehistoric machairodontine saber-toothed cat that lived in Eurasia, Africa and possibly North America from the late Pliocene to the Middle Pleistocene, first described by George Cuvier in 1824..

children.name: Profelis

children.name: Profelis aurata
children.description: The African golden cat (Caracal aurata) is a wild cat endemic to the rainforests of West and Central Africa.

children.description: Panthera balamoides ("similar to jaguar") is a possibly dubious species described as an extinct species of the big cat genus Panthera that is known from a single fossil found in a Late Pleistocene (Rancholabrean NALMA, dated to 13,000 BP) age cenote in the Yucatan Peninsula, Mexico.

children.name: Panthera gombaszoegensis
children.description: Panthera gombaszogensis, also known as the European jaguar or Eurasian jaguar, is a Panthera species that lived from about 2 million to 300,000 years ago in Europe, as well as likely elsewhere in Eurasia.

children.name: Panthera leo
children.description: The lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

children.name: Panthera onca
children.description: The jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.

children.name: Panthera palaeosinensis
children.description: Panthera palaeosinensis was an early Pleistocene species from northern China.

children.name: Panthera pardus
children.description: The leopard (Panthera pardus) is one of the five extant cat species in the genus Panthera.

children.name: Panthera spelaea
children.description: Panthera spelaea, commonly known as the cave lion (or less commonly as the steppe lion), is an extinct Panthera species that was native to Eurasia and northwest North America during the Pleistocene epoch.

children.name: Panthera tigris
children.description: The tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.

children.name: Panthera zdanskyi
children.description: Panthera zdanskyi is an extinct pantherine species, the fossils of which were excavated in Gansu Province, northwestern China.

children.name: Machairodus africanus
children.description: Machairodus (from Ancient Greek μάχαιρα (mákhaira), a type of ancient sword, and ὀδούς (odoús), meaning "tooth") is a genus of large machairodont or ''saber-toothed cat'' that lived in Africa and Eurasia during the Middle to Late Miocene, from 12.5 million to 8.7 million years ago..

children.name: Machairodus giganteus
children.description: Amphimachairodus (from Ancient Greek ἀμφί (amphí), meaning "both", μάχαιρα (mákhaira), a type of ancient sword, and ὀδούς (odoús), meaning "tooth") is an extinct genus of homotherin machairodontine felids..

children.description: Xenosmilus (from Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos), meaning "strange", and σμίλη (smílē), meaning "knife, chisel") is an extinct genus of homotherin machairodontine felid (saber-toothed cat) that roamed North America from the Early Pleistocene..

children.description: Metailurus is a genus of saber-toothed cat in the family Felidae, and belonging to the tribe Metailurini, which occurred in North America, Eurasia and Africa from the Miocene to the Middle Pleistocene..

children.name: Melursus ursinus
children.description: The sloth bear, also known as the Indian bear, is a myrmecophagous bear species native to the Indian subcontinent. It feeds on fruits, ants and termites. It is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, mainly because of habitat loss and degradation.

children.name: Ailuropoda
children.description: Ailuropoda — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Ailuropoda melanoleuca
children.description: The giant panda, also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China. It is characterised by its white coat with black patches around the eyes, ears, legs and shoulders. Its body is rotund; adult individuals weigh 100 to 115 kg and are typically 1.2 to 1.9 m long.

children.name: Ailuropoda microta
children.description: Ailuropoda microta is the earliest known member of the genus Ailuropoda, which includes the living giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca).

children.name: Tremarctos
children.description: Tremarctos — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Tremarctos ornatus
children.description: The spectacled bear, also known as the Andean bear, is a species of bear native to the Andes Mountains in northern and western South America. It is the only living species of bear native to South America, and the last remaining short-faced bear. Unlike other omnivorous bears, the diet of the spectacled bear is mostly herbivorous.

children.name: Helarctos
children.description: Helarctos — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Helarctos malayanus
children.description: The sun bear is a bear species in the family Ursidae found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia. It is the only species in the genus Helarctos and the smallest bear species, standing nearly 70 cm (28 in) at the shoulder and weighing 25–65 kg (55–143 lb). It is stockily built, with large paws, strongly curved claws, small, rounded ears and a short snout.

children.name: Ursus

children.name: Ursus abstrusus
children.description: Protarctos is an extinct genus of basal ursine bear that lived in North America and Eurasia during the Pliocene and into Early Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus americanus
children.description: The American black bear, or simply black bear, is a species of medium-sized bear which is endemic to North America. It is the continent's smallest and most widely distributed bear species. It is an omnivore, with a diet varying greatly depending on season and location.

children.name: Ursus arctos
children.description: The brown bear is a large bear native to Eurasia and North America. Of the land carnivorans, it is rivaled in size only by its closest relative, the polar bear, which is much less variable in size and slightly bigger on average. The brown bear is a sexually dimorphic species, as adult males are larger and more compactly built than females.

children.name: Ursus deningeri
children.description: Ursus deningeri (sometimes called Deninger's bear) is an extinct species of bear native to Eurasia from the late Early Pleistocene to the Middle Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus etruscus
children.description: Ursus etruscus, the Etruscan bear, is an extinct bear species that was native to Eurasia during the Early Pleistocene, living from approximately 2.2 million to around 1.4–1.2 million years ago.

children.name: Ursus ingressus
children.description: Ursus ingressus is an extinct species of the cave bear species complex that lived in Central Europe during the Late Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus maritimus
children.description: The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed. The polar bear is the largest extant species of bear and land carnivore by body mass, with adult males weighing 300–800 kg (660–1,760 lb).

children.name: Ursus minimus
children.description: Ursus minimus (the Auvergne bear) is an extinct species of bear, endemic to Europe during the Pliocene and Pleistocene, living from 5.3 to 1.8 Mya, existing for about .

children.name: Ursus spelaeus
children.description: The cave bear is a prehistoric species of bear that lived in Europe and Asia during the Pleistocene and became extinct about 24,000 years ago during the Last Glacial Maximum.

children.name: Ursus thibetanus
children.description: The Asian black bear (Ursus thibetanus), also known as the Asiatic black bear, moon bear and white-chested bear, is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia that is largely adapted to an arboreal lifestyle.

children.name: Ursus vitabilis
children.description: The American black bear (Ursus americanus), or simply black bear, is a species of medium-sized bear which is endemic to North America..

children.description: Hemicyon, also known as the "dog-bear" (literally "half dog", from Greek ἡμι- hēmi- (half) + κύων kúōn (dog)), is an extinct genus of hemicyonine bear, which probably originated in Eurasia but was found in Europe, Asia and North America during the Miocene epoch (15.97 to 12.75 million years ago), existing for approximately 16 to 13 mya..
